why: EVIDENCE (dashboard D: 120 s, 80 req/s, 9788 reqs; stable v1.0 x3 pods = 7404 reqs, canary v1.1 x1 pod = 2384 reqs, ~24% of traffic). Availability: canary 0 5xx / 2384 reqs = 0.00%, same as stable (0 / 7404). Central latency: canary p50 33 ms vs stable 35 ms, canary p95 95 ms vs stable 95 ms - no regression. Per endpoint the canary matches or beats stable on p50/p95: /browse 22/27 vs 22/27, /search 47/60 vs 47/59, /checkout 79/102 vs 82/103 (checkout, the revenue path, is marginally faster). Stability over time: canary p95 across the four 30 s windows is 95, 95, 92, 95 ms vs stable 96, 93, 94, 97 ms, and 5xx stays 0 in every window - no drift, no warm-up cliff, no late degradation. ONLY ANOMALY: tail latency. Canary overall p99 172 ms vs stable 104 ms, driven entirely by /search p99 652 ms vs stable 61 ms. JUDGEMENT on that anomaly: I treat it as a non-blocking tail artifact rather than a real regression, because (a) p99 over 729 canary /search requests is set by roughly the 7 slowest requests, so it is a very low-confidence statistic, (b) canary /search p50 and p95 are identical to stable (47 / 60 vs 47 / 59), which is inconsistent with a systemic slowdown and consistent with a few isolated slow requests such as single-pod cold start or cache/connection warm-up, and (c) none of those slow requests failed - error rate is still 0%. Blast radius: ~1% of /search on the canary is ~0.07% of total traffic, slow but successful, versus blocking a release on roughly 7 requests. LIMITS OF THE EVIDENCE (judgement): with 0/2384 observed failures the rule of three puts the 95% upper bound on canary error rate at ~0.13%, so a very small error rate cannot be excluded; there is also no CPU/memory/saturation data, no per-pod breakdown, only 120 s of observation, and the canary served ~25% of traffic as a single pod, so this does not prove behaviour at 4x the load. DECISION: promote, with conditions - ramp rather than jumping straight to 100% if the tooling allows, and watch /search p99 plus overall 5xx for the first several minutes at full traffic; roll back if /search p99 stays above ~200 ms once all pods are warm, or if 5xx exceeds 0.1% on any endpoint.
